trial_court: Court of Special Chief Judicial Magistrate (Customs) Lucknow
case_name: Santosh Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. S.O.P.O.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Santosh Kumar And 2 Others (husband, wife, plaintiff)
parties.respondent_defendant: State Of U.P. Thru. S.O.P.O., Mohanlalganj Lucknow And Anors. (wife, husband, defendant)

facts_of_case: The petitioners approached the court for quashing the charge sheet filed against them under Sections 498-A,323,504 and 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act. The parties had amicably settled their disputes and entered into compromise not to proceed further against each other.

legal_principles.principle: The continuance of proceedings will be misuse of the process of the Court when parties have amicably settled their disputes.
legal_principles.held: In view of Hon'ble the Supreme Court expressed in B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 Supreme Court Cases 675 the charge sheet should be quashed.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section X
cited_cases: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 Supreme Court Cases 675

legal_principles.principle: Proceedings should be quashed when parties have amicably settled their disputes and there is no further need for the Court to intervene.
legal_principles.held: The charge sheet should be quashed.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section X
cited_cases: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 Supreme Court Cases 675
keywords: no further need for the Court to intervene

outcome.final_order: The proceedings were quashed as the continuance of the same would be misuse of the process of the Court.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing a charge sheet
quashing a charge sheet in a magistrate court
